title: Practice Exam: Matter, Solutions, and Mixtures
description: 15-question practice exam covering classification of matter, solutions/colloids/suspensions, density, and molality calculations.

questions.question: Which of the following is a pure substance?
questions.explanation: Oxygen gas (O₂) is a pure substance consisting of only one type of element. Saltwater and air are homogeneous mixtures; bronze is a heterogeneous alloy.

questions.question: A 40 mL sample of a liquid has a mass of 36 g. What is its density?
Which characteristic is unique to colloids?
options: Can be separated by simple filtration
Display the Tyndall effect when light passes through
questions.explanation: Colloids display the Tyndall effect because their particles (1 nm-1 μm) are large enough to scatter light. Solutions do not show this effect; suspensions settle quickly; and colloids cannot be filtered like suspensions.

questions.question: Which of the following would sink in water (density of water = 1.0 g/mL)?
questions.explanation: Objects sink if their density is greater than the liquid's density. Aluminum (2.7 g/mL) > water (1.0 g/mL), so it sinks. All other options have densities less than water and float.

questions.question: Classify milk.
questions.explanation: Milk is a colloid—an opaque homogeneous-appearing mixture with fat globules (1 nm-1 μm) dispersed in water. It exhibits the Tyndall effect but does not settle like a suspension.

questions.question: A student shines a laser through two liquids. Liquid A shows a bright beam path (Tyndall effect); Liquid B shows no beam. What can be concluded?
options: Liquid A is a solution; Liquid B is a colloid
Liquid A is a colloid; Liquid B is a solution
questions.explanation: The Tyndall effect occurs in colloids because particles scatter light. If Liquid A shows the Tyndall effect, it is a colloid. Liquid B does not scatter light, so it is a solution or pure liquid.

questions.question: What is the molality of a solution prepared by dissolving 5.85 g of NaCl (molar mass = 58.5 g/mol) in 500 g of water?
questions.explanation: Moles of NaCl = 5.85 g / 58.5 g/mol = 0.1 mol; Mass of water = 500 g = 0.5 kg; Molality = 0.1 mol / 0.5 kg = 0.2 m. Wait, let me recalculate: Actually 0.1 mol / 0.5 kg = 0.2 m. questions.question: Which separation technique would be most effective for separating components of a solution with different boiling points?
questions.explanation: Distillation separates liquid components based on differences in boiling point. Filtration is for suspensions; centrifugation and evaporation serve other purposes.

questions.question: True or False: A solution can be separated by passing it through filter paper.
questions.explanation: False. Solutions have particles < 1 nm, which pass through filter paper. Only suspensions with particles > 1 μm can be separated by filtration.

questions.question: True or False: Molality is independent of temperature.
questions.explanation: True. Molality is moles of solute per kilogram of solvent, both of which are mass-based. Temperature changes do not affect mass, so molality remains constant. This is why molality is preferred for colligative property calculations.

questions.question: True or False: All clear, transparent liquids are solutions.
questions.explanation: False. Some colloids appear transparent or slightly opaque but still display the Tyndall effect. Pure liquids are also transparent. The Tyndall effect test is needed to distinguish colloids from solutions.

questions.question: A liquid sample has a mass of 60 g and a volume of 50 mL. Its density is _____ g/mL.
Calculate the molality of a solution containing 11.7 g of KCl (molar mass = 74.5 g/mol) dissolved in 200 g of water. The answer is _____ m.
questions.explanation: Moles of KCl = 11.7 g / 74.5 g/mol = 0.157 mol; Mass of water = 200 g = 0.2 kg; Molality = 0.157 mol / 0.2 kg = 0.785 m

questions.question: Explain why suspensions settle over time while solutions and colloids do not.
acceptableAnswers: Suspensions have large particles (>1 μm) that are affected by gravity and settle. Solutions have very small particles (<1 nm) that remain dispersed due to random molecular motion (Brownian motion). Colloids have intermediate-sized particles (1 nm-1 μm) that are large enough to be affected by some settling forces but small enough to stay suspended for extended periods due to Brownian motion.
The particles in suspensions are large and heavy enough to overcome forces keeping them dispersed, causing them to settle by gravity.
questions.explanation: Particle size determines settling behavior. Larger particles in suspensions are pulled down by gravity faster than smaller particles in solutions and colloids can be kept dispersed by Brownian motion.

questions.question: A chemist needs to identify whether an unknown clear liquid is a solution or a pure liquid. Describe an experiment using a laser pointer to make this determination.
acceptableAnswers: Shine a laser pointer through the liquid. If a bright red beam is visible (Tyndall effect), the liquid is likely a colloid. If no beam is visible, it is a solution or pure liquid. However, this test cannot definitively distinguish between a solution and a pure liquid.
Direct a laser beam through the sample. Observe if light scatters (visible beam) indicating a colloid, or if light passes through without scattering (solution or pure liquid).
questions.explanation: The Tyndall effect (visible laser beam) indicates colloidal particles that scatter light. A solution does not scatter light visibly. However, this test cannot distinguish between a solution and a pure liquid.
